limitations_and_boundaries: DeepONet accuracy is bounded by the numerical solver used to generate training data.
Training DeepONets is computationally intensive because the dataset size is the product of the number of input functions and evaluation locations.
Theoretical understanding of why DeepONets induce small generalization errors is lacking.
No theoretical bounds on network size for operator approximation are available.
The study uses fully connected subnetworks; other architectures like CNNs or attention may improve accuracy but are not fully explored.
The work focuses on operators with known mathematical forms; discovering operators from multi-fidelity or heterogeneous data is left for future work.

experiments_or_tasks: Design two versions of DeepONet: stacked and unstacked, with branch and trunk subnetworks.
Evaluate DeepONet on 16 test cases including integrals, Legendre transforms, fractional derivatives, nonlinear ODEs/PDEs, and stochastic ODEs/PDEs.
Propose a general deep learning framework, DeepONet, to learn diverse continuous nonlinear operators.
Prove a generalized universal approximation theorem for operators (Theorem 2) that allows deep branch/trunk networks.

methods.name: DeepONet
methods.protocol_description: DeepONet consists of a branch net encoding the discrete input function [u(x1),...,u(xm)] and a trunk net encoding the output location y. The output is the dot product of branch and trunk outputs plus a bias. Two versions: stacked (p separate branch nets) and unstacked (single branch net outputting p-dimensional vector). Loss function is mean squared error between true G(u)(y) and prediction. Implemented in DeepXDE.
